geometry.derivationNote: The 1868 secret supplement expressly frames the emir's obligations as a sign of his wish to acquire the protection of the Russian Emperor, while the peace terms leave Bukhara as a distinct polity. This verifies a Russian protection/dependency relationship on the claim/sphere-of-control track. It does not justify treating Bukhara as core Russian sovereign territory or asserting a geometry-bearing annexation.

territoryChanges.notes: Legacy id retained for compatibility. `protectorate` here denotes the source-backed protection/dependency relationship recorded by the 1868 settlement; it is not a claim that a single treaty article created an ordinary territorial protectorate identical to direct Russian sovereignty.

effectiveDate.note: This change is narrowed to the initial 1868 Samarkand/Zarafshan acquisition evidenced by the peace settlement. Later Penjikent and 1870–1871 upper-Zarafshan/Kashkadarya additions require separate dated acts.

routeSemantics.source: peace conditions state this boundary was to be fixed precisely after acceptance

geometry.derivationNote: The initial 1868 legal acquisition and its boundary grammar are source-verified. Exact polygon geometry still requires the subsequent boundary-fixing documentation and period survey/cartography. The former broad 1868–1870 range has been removed because it conflated later expansions with the initial acquisition.

territoryChanges.notes: Exact monthly transition resolved for the initial acquisition only. Later additions are not silently backdated to 5 July 1868.

geometry.derivationNote: Article 1 places Khiva's direct foreign relations, treaty-making and military action under Russian authority. This is represented as a dependent-polity/control sphere, not as core Russian territory. The treaty does not justify filling the whole khanate as Russian sovereign territory.

territoryChanges.notes: The dependency status and the direct right-bank territorial acquisition are intentionally separate changes.

routeSemantics.feature: southern Ust-Urt chink / old Amu channel

geometry.derivationNote: Articles 2-3 source-verify both the route grammar and the transfer of all right-bank Khivan lands to Russia. Exact geometry requires historical Amu Darya distributaries, the 1873 Aral shoreline, the identification of Kukertli/Cape Urgu and the old Amu channel; modern hydrography must not be substituted.

The RGVIA original/PSZRI decree source-verifies the legal inclusion of the territory constituting the former Kokand Khanate and creation of Fergana Oblast. The 1876 Asian Department of the General Staff map is the contemporary official geometry source, but the historical oblast/khanate boundary must be georeferenced and reconciled with adjacent treaty boundaries before polygon promotion.

territoryChanges.notes: Legal territorial transition is source-verified; geometry remains dependent on the contemporary official map rather than a modern Fergana administrative outline.
